method: The top 10 nodes by PageRank on the call subgraph were rated by reading the referenced source in data/repos/fa1df9ec-61f6-4497-ab7d-184bbc30aee5. 'core' means the node is load-bearing in Flask's public machinery (request lifecycle, routing, globals, setup-time safety). 'peripheral' means it is useful but not on the hot path: examples, specific-case helpers.
target_rule: at least 7 of 10 top-PageRank nodes judged 'core'

ratings.rationale: Blueprint deferred-setup primitive; every blueprint call eventually goes through record / record_once.
Lives under /examples/tutorial, not Flask proper. Only tutorial code calls it, but it has many callers inside that example.
Internal helper behind Scaffold.get / .post / .put etc. — every method-shortcut goes through it.
One specific JSON serializer helper for tagged types in the signed-session path; not on the typical request hot path.
Called for every view invocation; handles async-view wrapping. Central to Flask's dispatch.
The @app.route decorator itself. Can't be more core than this.
Backbone of every LocalProxy access (request, session, current_app, g). Reached millions of times per request.
The decorator guarding all setup-time methods (route, before_request, register_blueprint…) against post-boot mutation.
The closure setupmethod returns; every protected setup call runs through here.
